title: Erlang latency statistics
context: Summarises request latencies given as integer microseconds for a dashboard that shows milliseconds. summary/1 returns #{count, mean_ms, p95_ms, max_ms}, with all zeros for an empty list. p95 uses nearest rank: the element at 1-based rank ceil(0.95 * N) of the sorted samples. merge/2 combines two summaries; its mean must equal the mean over all underlying samples and p95 becomes undefined.
code: #{count => N, mean_ms => Mean, p95_ms => P95, max_ms => Max}.
merge(#{count := C1, mean_ms := M1, max_ms := X1}, #{count := C2, mean_ms := M2, max_ms := X2}) ->
#{count => Count, mean_ms => Mean, p95_ms => undefined, max_ms => max(X1, X2)}.
format(#{count := N, mean_ms := Mean, p95_ms := P95, max_ms := Max}) ->
io_lib:format("n=~b mean=~p ms p95=~p ms max=~p ms", [N, Mean, P95, Max]).

expected.why: nearest rank needs ceil; trunc picks the wrong element and gives rank 0 for fewer than 20 samples, so lists:nth crashes
p95 is returned in microseconds while the other fields are converted to milliseconds
the two means are averaged without weighting by count, so the result is not the mean of all samples; use (M1 * C1 + M2 * C2) / Count
